claim_scope: A furnished room with dense coordinated layering across ceiling, curtains, upholstery, floor, lighting and objects. The publisher explicitly discusses this photographed room as maximalism; this is not a universal recipe or an exclusive historical movement identity.
limits: One published room view; no complete-house survey, material authentication, comfort or accessibility testing. The caption spells the house “Dawnbridge”; it refers to Tony Duquette’s house associated with Hutton Wilkinson. Photograph date, exact pictured interior-version date, individual photographers and the authorship of every object are not established by this excerpt. Dense collections are part of this room’s designed layering, not evidence that arbitrary clutter or luxury automatically establishes Maximalism.
observable_features: A complete furnished room view places a pale sofa and glass table within patterned side chairs, a foreground spotted chair, hanging cages, plants and decorative objects.
Blue swirling motifs recur on curtains and armchairs, while green ceiling, framing and foliage connect the layers across the room.
Ceiling lattice, shaped cornice, branching chandelier, cage outlines and plants create distinct overlapping scales above the seating area.
A large black-and-white diagonal floor grid contrasts with a patterned stair covering and multiple upholstery patterns, while the central table and sofa remain an identifiable focus.
No visitors, explanatory text, watermarks or gallery equipment are included in the extracted photograph.

association_evidence.supports: The inspected publisher sample, printed pp. 48–49 (PDF page index 7), pairs this exact photograph with a discussion headed Maximum Maximalism and identifies Tony Duquette’s house, now associated with Hutton Wilkinson. The caption describes repeated fabric, lattice, hanging birdcages, colors, textures and coordinated layers. This supports the room/image association and author’s style reading, not every object’s age or authorship.

confusion_check.shared_appearances: Mixed collections, rich patterns, plants and ornament can also occur in bohemian rooms, historical revivals or incidental clutter.
confusion_check.discriminating_relationships: Repeated blue motifs and green links coordinate otherwise different patterns and object types; the floor, ceiling, upholstery and hanging layers surround a readable seating focus. This whole-room coordination is more diagnostic than counting objects or requiring historical Rococo forms. A bohemian or revival influence may coexist rather than being ruled out.
confusion_check.cannot_conclude: The image cannot establish the entire house’s style, a furnishing’s provenance, comfort, cost, personal psychology or that every busy room is intentionally maximalist.

retrieval_method: Public publisher PDF downloaded normally. Its native RGB JPEG image stream was extracted without recompression, resizing, retouching or cropping and matched visually to a PDFKit-rendered source page.
image_transformation: No image-pixel change: original embedded RGB JPEG preserved. Text and page furniture are separate PDF objects and are not part of this native photograph.
